title: Best Workday Competitors & Alternatives (2026 Updated)
summary: Compare the best Workday competitors, including brioHR, Darwinbox, and HiBob. Explore HR, payroll, HCM, pricing, features, and enterprise alternatives.
body_markdown:
Key Takeaways


- **brioHR** is best for mid-market and SME teams in Malaysia and Singapore that want an all-in-one HRMS without Workday's enterprise price tag or rollout timeline.
- **Darwinbox** is best for large Asia-based enterprises that still need enterprise-grade scale, just with native regional payroll Workday doesn't offer out of the box.
- **HiBob** is best for global mid-market to enterprise teams that weight culture, engagement, and learning and development as heavily as core HR admin.
- One analysis of enterprise rollouts found that Workday implementations run with average timelines of 8.2 months and costs ranging from $300K to $800K, plus annual fees of $40 to $160 per employee per month, which is why so many mid-market teams start looking elsewhere before they've even finished onboarding.


Workday still dominates conversations about enterprise HR software, but it wasn't built for every company that finds itself comparing it. This guide breaks down nine platforms worth considering instead, what each one actually does well, where it falls short, and who it's genuinely built for.


## Introduction


If you've been quoted a Workday implementation and the number made you close the laptop, you're not overreacting. A platform designed for organizations running 10,000-plus employees across a dozen countries carries a price tag and rollout timeline to match, and most companies evaluating HR software today aren't that. They're mid-market teams in Malaysia or Singapore, regional offices of larger groups, or SMEs that outgrew spreadsheets but never needed an enterprise resource planning suite bolted onto their HR function.


This article compares nine Workday alternatives across pricing, features, and who each one actually fits, so you can find a platform sized to your company rather than one built for a Fortune 500 rollout.

## brioHR: Best for MY/SG Mid-Market Teams Wanting a Right-Sized Alternative


brioHR is an all-in-one HRMS covering recruitment, onboarding, payroll, leave, claims, time and attendance, performance, and engagement in one connected system. It's used by more than 1,000 organizations across 50 countries, with the bulk of that client base sitting in the 30 to 3,000 employee range that Workday's enterprise pricing and rollout model typically prices out.


Where Workday asks companies to adapt to enterprise-grade complexity, brioHR is built around the opposite premise: one system, sized for how mid-market HR teams in Malaysia and Singapore actually operate.


### brioHR Key Features


brioHR's feature set spans the full employee lifecycle, but three areas stand out most clearly against Workday for mid-market buyers: connected performance management, built-in reporting, and native regional payroll.


#### Performance Management Connected to Real Employee Data


brioHR's[performance management](https://briohr.com/products/performance-management/) module runs full review cycles, 360-degree feedback, self-assessments, peer reviews, and continuous check-ins on the same employee record as payroll and attendance data. That matters more than it sounds like on paper: a manager reviewing someone's year doesn't have to cross-reference a separate system to see attendance patterns or comp history.


> "it's not necessary to have a super advanced process. What's important is to have something. And I actually am an advocate of simpler, better."


**[Benjamin Croc, Co-Founder and CEO of brioHR](https://my.linkedin.com/in/benjamin-croc-93669426)


For a company evaluating Workday's much heavier performance suite, that's a genuinely different starting point.


#### HR Reporting and People Analytics


Instead of a separate business intelligence layer bolted onto HR data, brioHR's[reporting and analytics tools](https://briohr.com/products/hr-reporting-software/) include custom report builders, headcount dashboards, attrition analytics, and scheduled report emails, all pulling from the same core employee dataset. For teams that have relied on manual spreadsheet exports until now, this is often the single biggest efficiency gain, and it's worth reading through[what to look for in people analytics software](https://briohr.com/blog/people-analytics-software/) if reporting depth is your main reason for shopping.


#### Native Malaysia and Singapore Payroll


Unlike Workday, where Malaysia and Singapore compliance sits on top of a global framework rather than being native to it, brioHR's[payroll module](https://briohr.com/my/products/payroll/) handles EPF, SOCSO, EIS, LHDN, CPF, SDL, IR8A, and IR21 as core functionality, with statutory updates rolling out automatically rather than requiring a support ticket.


### brioHR Pricing

### Where brioHR Shines


- **One platform instead of five:** Payroll, leave, claims, attendance, performance, and reporting connect in one system, cutting the duplicate data entry that comes with stitching tools together.
- **Malaysia and Singapore compliance handled natively:** EPF, SOCSO, EIS, LHDN, CPF, SDL, IR8A, and IR21 all work out of the box, with statutory updates applied automatically.
- **Support that actually responds:** Sub-three-minute average response times and a 96% positive feedback rate, which matters a lot more once payroll deadlines are involved.


### Where brioHR Falls Short


- **Not built for very small teams:** A company with fewer than about 30 employees may not use enough of the platform's breadth to justify the switch from simpler point tools.
- **Smaller learning and development suite than global HCM platforms:** Certification tracking and skills matrices exist only partially, so companies that need a full course catalog and LMS will still want a dedicated L&D tool alongside it.

## Darwinbox: Best for Large Enterprises Across Asia


Darwinbox is an enterprise HR platform built for larger organizations, particularly across Asia. It's the closest genuine peer to Workday in scale and ambition, with one meaningful difference: native Malaysia and Singapore payroll built in from the start, rather than configured after the fact.


### Key Features


- **Native regional payroll:** Full EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB, HRDF, CPF, SDL, and IR8A support, a real gap in Workday's regional coverage.
- **Mature talent and L&D suite:** OKRs, KPI tracking, succession planning, e-learning, and skills matrices are all built in, not add-ons.
- **Enterprise-scale analytics:** Predictive analytics, attrition analysis, and custom report builders designed for large headcounts.


### Pricing


Plan Details


Enterprise Custom quote, premium tier, typically out of reach for SMEs and smaller mid-market companies


### Where Darwinbox Shines


- **Faster rollout than Workday for a comparable scale:** Implementation typically runs three to six months, well under Workday's 8.2-month average.
- **Regional payroll depth most global platforms skip:** A genuine differentiator against Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, and other global HCM suites operating in Southeast Asia.
- **Mature talent management:** Succession planning and calibration tools that hold up against Workday's equivalent modules.


### Where Darwinbox Falls Short


- **Partial Malaysian compliance depth:** EA Form, LHDN e-filing, and religious leave types are only partially supported, and HRDF/SBL-Khas tracking is missing entirely.
- **Overbuilt for mid-sized teams:** Designed for enterprise complexity that can feel heavy for organizations under about 500 employees.
- **No payroll outsourcing service:** Companies wanting managed payroll alongside the software need a separate provider.


### Darwinbox Customer Reviews


[RR Rafael R. Program Manager ★★★★☆ 4.5 "Comprehensive HR Solution with Seamless Integrations"](https://www.g2.com/products/darwinbox/reviews/darwinbox-review-12600554)[SP Shivendra P. Product Analyst ★★★★☆ 3.5 "Great UI and QR Punching, But Punch Errors and Frequent Updates Can Frustrate"](https://www.g2.com/products/darwinbox/reviews/darwinbox-review-13322077)


### Who Darwinbox Is Best For


Large enterprises and regional organizations across Asia that need Workday-level scale and talent management depth, and can absorb enterprise pricing plus a multi-month rollout. For teams weighing that trade-off, it's worth reading[how to choose HR software in Singapore](https://briohr.com/blog/a-guide-to-choosing-hr-software-singapore/) before committing to either platform.


## HiBob: Best for Culture-First Global Teams


HiBob (Bob) targets modern, culture-driven companies typically running 100 to 5,000-plus employees. On paper, it carries the most complete performance and learning suite of any alternative in this comparison, closer to Workday's depth than most mid-market tools attempt.


### Key Features


- **Full performance and succession suite:** Goal setting, 360-degree feedback, calibration, PIP workflows, and the only true native succession planning outside Darwinbox and Workday.
- **Deepest L&D suite in this comparison:** Full course catalog, certification tracking, and skills matrix.
- **Culture and engagement tools:** Recognition, internal messaging, and pulse surveys sit alongside the performance suite, an area worth comparing against[why businesses run employee pulse surveys](https://briohr.com/blog/why-run-employee-pulse-surveys/) if engagement is a priority.


### Pricing


Plan Details


Pricing model Quote-based, no published rate


Typical range Roughly $16–25 per employee per month, plus a 10–20% implementation fee


### Where HiBob Shines


- **Most complete performance checklist outside Workday and Darwinbox:** Native succession planning alongside calibration and PIP workflows.
- **Strongest L&D suite in this comparison:** Course catalog, certification tracking, and skills matrix, features most mid-market alternatives don't offer at all.
- **High overall satisfaction:** 4.6 out of 5 on Capterra from 179 verified reviews.


### Where HiBob Falls Short


- **No native Malaysia or Singapore payroll:** Regional teams need a separate local payroll provider, undercutting one of the main reasons to leave Workday in the first place.
- **Performance tools feel thinner in practice than the feature list suggests:** Reviewers report the actual experience needs work, particularly around competency frameworks.
- **Pricing isn't transparent:** Quote-based with an added implementation fee makes it harder to budget upfront than platforms with published rates.

Global and multi-national companies from 100 to 5,000-plus employees that don't need Malaysia or Singapore statutory payroll, and want engagement and L&D depth weighted as heavily as core performance tracking.


## Employment Hero: Best for Broad HR and Payroll Coverage


Employment Hero is built around a wide HR and payroll ecosystem, better suited to companies wanting payroll as part of a broader HR stack than a tightly integrated payroll-first system. It's strongest in Australia and the UK, so Southeast Asian teams should weigh localization depth carefully against Workday's global reach.


### Key Features


- **Wide platform coverage:** Recruitment, onboarding, performance, payroll, and reporting all live in the same ecosystem.
- **360-degree feedback inside the performance module:** Not a standalone product, but genuinely present.
- **Employee self-service portal:** Reduces routine admin for both employees and HR, a benefit worth checking against the broader[reasons companies use HR software](https://briohr.com/blog/reasons-why-companies-use-hr-software/) .


### Pricing


Plan Details


HR Premium From USD $10 per employee per month, subject to a USD $100 minimum monthly contract


Malaysia guidance Around RM8–12 per employee per month, RM160–240 monthly minimum


### Where Employment Hero Shines


- **Wide feature breadth for the price:** Recruitment through payroll in one ecosystem, more horizontal coverage than most alternatives at this price point.
- **Modern employee self-service experience:** A genuine improvement over the manual processes it replaces.


### Where Employment Hero Falls Short


- **Payroll and HR aren't fully unified:** Payroll was acquired separately, and it shows in a separate login and occasional friction between modules.
- **Weaker Malaysia and Singapore localization than regional-native tools:** Support depth and compliance coverage can be inconsistent, and implementation typically takes around six months.

## Swingvy: Best for SMEs Modernizing HR for the First Time


Swingvy pairs HR admin and payroll in a clean, mobile-first package, usually chosen by SMEs moving off spreadsheets without wanting to step straight into anything close to Workday's complexity.


### Key Features


- **Modern mobile experience:** iOS and Android apps for leave, claims, and clock-in, which drives adoption across the whole company rather than just HR.
- **Core HR and payroll:** Full Malaysian statutory support (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB, HRDF, LHDN) alongside leave, claims, and employee records.
- **Shift-based attendance:** Mobile GPS clock-in, geo-fencing, and shift scheduling suited to distributed teams, an area also covered in[how HRMS tools transform productivity measurement](https://briohr.com/blog/hrms-tools/) .


### Pricing

- **Cleaner UX than most legacy local tools:** Independent comparisons rate the interface at 4.0 out of 5.
- **Good fit for distributed and shift-based teams:** Mobile clock-in and geo-fencing work well outside a single office location.


### Where Swingvy Falls Short


- **Light performance management:** No OKRs, KPI tracking, 360 feedback, or succession planning, features that matter if you're comparing against Workday's talent suite.

## PayrollPanda: Best for Payroll-First Micro-SMEs


PayrollPanda is a payroll-first platform built for Malaysian SMEs, known for simple processing and a free plan that genuinely covers unlimited payroll runs. It pairs with Jibble for time and attendance rather than building that in natively.


### Key Features


- **Payroll automation:** Salary calculations, payslips, and statutory deductions handled automatically.
- **Statutory compliance:** EPF, SOCSO, PCB support, plus EA Form and Form E.
- **Basic HR coverage:** Employee records and leave, kept intentionally simple.

- **A free plan that actually delivers:** Unlimited payroll runs and statutory support at no cost, rare for the Malaysian market and a stark contrast to Workday's six-figure entry point.
- **Responsive support:** Users frequently call out fast, helpful responses.


### Where PayrollPanda Falls Short


- **Narrow product scope:** Beyond payroll, leave, and basic time tracking, separate tools are needed for claims, performance, onboarding, and recruitment.
- **Payroll built for Malaysia only:** No multi-currency, regional, or outsourced payroll option for cross-border teams.
- **No custom report builder or people analytics:** Reporting stays basic even on paid tiers.

## Reasons to Find a Competitor to Workday


Workday earned its enterprise reputation, but that reputation comes with trade-offs that matter a lot more once you're the one signing the contract.


### The Implementation Timeline Doesn't Match Your Runway


Enterprise Workday deployments run with average timelines of 8.2 months, and complex, multi-entity rollouts can stretch well past a year. For a mid-market team that needs payroll running correctly next quarter, not next year, that timeline alone rules Workday out. Platforms sized for mid-market complexity, like brioHR, typically implement in about two months.


### The Cost Structure Assumes Enterprise Budgets


Between costs ranging from $300K to $800K, plus annual fees of $40 to $160 per employee per month, Workday's pricing model is built around companies that can absorb that spend without blinking. Modular, per-employee pricing from platforms like brioHR (starting at RM3 per employee per month) makes the same category of software accessible to teams an order of magnitude smaller.


### Regional Compliance Is Configured, Not Native


Workday's Malaysia and Singapore statutory support exists, but it's layered onto a global framework rather than built around EPF, SOCSO, EIS, LHDN, CPF, SDL, IR8A, and IR21 from the ground up. That gap is exactly where regionally native platforms, including brioHR, tend to close deals against Workday for Southeast Asian buyers.


Compare regional-native alternatives against[expense management systems](https://briohr.com/blog/best-expense-management-systems/) ,[employee engagement software](https://briohr.com/blog/best-employee-engagement-software/) , and[HR software in Singapore](https://briohr.com/blog/best-hr-software-singapore/) if you're evaluating multiple categories at once.

## How We Selected These Workday Competitors and Alternatives


We evaluated platforms against three criteria that matter most for teams actually comparing Workday to something else.


### Genuine Feature Overlap With Workday's Core Modules


Every tool on this list needed to cover at least some combination of Workday's core areas: HR admin, payroll, performance management, and reporting, rather than being a single-purpose point solution. That's why platforms like Darwinbox and HiBob, which carry genuine talent management depth, sit alongside more focused regional tools like Kakitangan and PayrollPanda that compete on cost and simplicity instead. For a deeper look at how these platforms stack up on reporting specifically, see our[reporting software comparison](https://briohr.com/blog/top-hr-reporting-software/) .


### Real, Published Pricing or a Clear Quote Path


We included pricing for every platform on this list, using published rates where available and clearly marking custom-quote models where they aren't. Workday's own pricing opacity is one of the top complaints buyers raise, so we didn't want to replicate that here.


### Verified Reviews and Honest Trade-Offs


Every platform's shines and falls-short sections reflect genuine trade-offs, not marketing copy. Where a platform has a real gap (no Singapore payroll, no recruitment module, thinner reporting), we said so directly rather than softening it.


## Final Word on brioHR


If you're comparing Workday alternatives because the price or timeline doesn't fit your company, and you're operating in Malaysia or Singapore, brioHR is worth a serious look. It covers the same core ground (payroll, performance, reporting, compliance) in one connected system, sized for a two-month rollout instead of eight.


That said, it's not the right fit for every reader here. If you're running a 10,000-person global enterprise with complex multi-country finance needs, Darwinbox or Workday itself may still be the more complete answer. If you're a five-person team that just needs clean payroll, PayrollPanda's free tier will get you further for less.

#### FAQs


1


** ** Who is Workday's biggest competitor?


No single platform dominates every use case. Darwinbox is the closest enterprise-tier peer for Asia-based companies, while SAP SuccessFactors and Oracle HCM Cloud compete most directly for global enterprise deals outside the region.


2


** ** Is ADP or Workday better?


It depends on the need. ADP is generally stronger for payroll-first companies and smaller headcounts, while Workday offers broader HCM functionality for large, complex global enterprises willing to pay for it.


3


** ** Is Workday being replaced by AI?


No, not entirely. Workday has added AI features for tasks like recruiting and analytics, but the platform itself remains the system of record. AI is supplementing specific workflows within it, not replacing the underlying HCM system.


4


** ** How long does it typically take to switch from Workday to a smaller HR platform?


Sometimes, migrations can take as little as two to three months for mid-market platforms with straightforward data exports, though timelines vary based on integration complexity and how much historical data needs to move.


5


** ** Do smaller Workday alternatives support multi-country payroll?


Sometimes. Platforms like Darwinbox and OmniHR support multi-country payroll within Southeast Asia specifically, but most regionally focused alternatives, including brioHR, are built primarily around Malaysia and Singapore rather than full global payroll coverage.
